text:
sarah: quick follow-up on yesterday's RFC — what do we want to do about unscoped API keys that currently default to org-level access? we've seen a few edge cases where keys get used across projects and audits are messy.

tom: +1 we should avoid silent defaults. i'm leaning to disallow unscoped keys for customer-facing APIs. org-scoped keys ok only with explicit admin opt-in + extra audit hooks. migration path required.

juan: migration path is the hard part. proposal: 1) emit warnings and tag existing unscoped keys for 30d, 2) provide an API to mint project-scoped equivalents, 3) if caller includes X-Project-Id header, prefer that mapping. avoid breaking webhooks in one go.

mira: product concern — third-party integrators rely on org tokens. can we offer a compatibility token type that is read-only + TTL-limited + rate-limited? less secure but lowers churn.

oliver: from an audit/forensics POV, if we keep any org-scoped keys we MUST attach lineage metadata (creator, linked service principal) and last_used_project in logs. otherwise post-incident attribution is impossible.

Tom: proposed policy snippet (draft):
```json
{
  "allow_unscoped_keys": false,
  "compatibility_mode": {
    "enabled": true,
    "features": ["readonly", "ttl", "rate_limit"]
  },
  "migration": {
    "warning_window_days": 30,
    "enforce_after_days": 90
  }
}
```

sarah: also thinking about runtime fallbacks — we should NOT have auth-layer fallback to an org-token when project capacity is exhausted. that's dangerous and hides failures. prefer routing policies at the service layer (canary to org-model only under controlled config).

juan: implementation note for authz: check `X-Project-Id` header first, then token scopes. If token has multiple scopes, require explicit mapping table lookup. Reject if ambiguous. Keep the authz check simple and deterministic.

mira: ops/comms: how do we signal this to customers? i'd do console banners + api response headers + targeted emails for keys used in multiple projects. also provide a one-click migration (mint project-key) in console.

deploy-bot: deployed RFC addendum link: https://go/internal/rfcs/1937 (adds migration job ENGSEC-4521)

sarah: next steps — i'll draft a short RFC addendum covering: migration timeline (30d warn, 90d enforcement), compatibility-token semantics, and required audit fields. @mira can you draft comms and a sample migration script?

mira: on it. will produce draft comms + a small CLI script for bulk migration.

oliver: :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks all — moving this to action items on the RFC thread.
